The dragons are dying, victims of merciless attacks by a foreign clan. The dragon council, desperate to replace the females they've lost, uncover eighteen-year-old Maayin - the last female capable of breeding a full-blooded dragon. Maayin, who has spent her life far from any dragon, is horrified by the claim that, despite her human appearance, she is a dragon. She agrees to go with them on one condition: they must bring her home when they're proven wrong. The old dragons laugh at her demands but a younger dragon, Jaimin, agrees.

Once imprisoned in the mountain lair, the evidence against Maayin quickly mounts up. Still, she struggles to believe the truth. Then she begins having feelings for Jaimin, who teaches her to accept her dragon heritage and, for the first time, Maayin feels like she belongs. Although ancient law deems it too dangerous for their two kinds to breed, being unable to choose Jaimin as her mate is only the beginning of Maayin's troubles.

Sixteen year old Gareth Wheatson runs from the only life he has ever known with a pack on his back and a single bright idea, become an adventurer, see the wider world, never return to the farm.

His first quest should have been simple. Clear a cave. Earn coin. Prove himself.

Instead he stumbles into a necromancer’s ritual and wakes as the thing every fireside story warns about, a lich.

Now Gareth is starving for soul energy, terrified of what he might do if he slips, and hunted by the church that would rather burn him than ask how it happened. He clings to one stubborn hope, reach the eastern port, catch a boat to the mainland, and vanish into a bigger world where an unwanted monster might still find a place to exist.

Getting there means surviving the road with his best friend James, dodging patrols and curfews, and hiding in plain sight among travellers who would panic if they knew what walked beside them. It means wolves in the dark, bandits on lonely tracks, and the constant risk of discovery every time Gareth’s hunger flares near living people.

As the net tightens and the church closes in, Gareth is forced to use powers he never wanted, and to decide what matters more, keeping his secret, or keeping the people he cares about alive

Dragons vanished three hundred years ago.

At least, that’s what the Church wants everyone to believe.

Ryan Vale was never meant to become anyone important. He was only a blacksmith’s apprentice in a forgotten border town—until the village’s mad old man, dying in his arms, pressed an ancient key into his hand and warned him never to give it to the Church.

Following the clue left behind by the key, Ryan entered a tomb sealed for three hundred years.

There, he found something that should no longer exist.

A dragon egg.

The last one.

Now the Church is hunting him, powerful kingdoms would do anything to seize what he carries, and the dragon waiting inside that egg may hate dragon riders more than anyone alive.

To survive, Ryan must uncover the truth behind the war that erased dragons from history, walk the forgotten path of the dragon riders, and earn the trust of a creature that was never meant to obey him.

Because if the last dragon takes to the skies again…

the world will remember why it once feared dragons.

Sixteen-year-old Thenio Iterune has a simple plan for his life: Work hard. Do well in school. Become a qualified wizard. Earn a good living. And maybe even make his parents proud of him someday.

Unfortunately, the plan isn't going too well....

Thenio's magic power is becoming increasingly difficult to control, which leads to a series of accidents that are about to cost him his hard-earned spot at the Kafron Royal Academy of Magic. And things don't get any better when he finally discovers the source of his problems: He has an extremely rare and unstable magic affinity. And it's going to do more than just get him expelled. It's probably going to get him killed.

Before he knows it, Thenio has gone from diligent student to disabled dropout. And forget about career plans...he'll be lucky if he even lives long enough to need a job in the first place.

Enter Iggy, a tiny black dragon who loves chasing birds and has a remarkable nose for magic. He takes an immediate liking to the scent of Thenio's unique magic and convinces his wizard partner, Ariom, to help find a way to stabilize it.

Are a genius enchanter and his slightly crazy dragon familiar enough to keep a chronically explosive boy alive? Maybe. But that's before demons get added into the mix....

Updates are irregular at the moment, but I'll get back to a weekly schedule as soon as I can.

Isaac is reincarnated in a new world, a young world that is untouched by gods and mortals alike.
With no humans, elves, or gods in existence yet, Isaac finds himself as the only intelligent being in the world.
He must navigate life as the first dragon, discovering what it means to exist in a land shaped by raw magic.
Follow him as he lives out the life of a dragon, as days become weeks and weeks become years.

How old can a dragon become? How long is a dragon nap? Guess Isaac will have to find that out.

Dragon Days is simple: as time goes on, Isaac will explore what it means to be a dragon in a world of magic and witness the rise of mortals and gods in a new world.

Ooo, and there is a system, and levels.

Chapter release: 1 a week, usually Friday, or Thursday  (and a surprise drop here and there)

This is a story of how a powerless man thrown about in a world he had no say in, unable to do anything about his circumstances and a victim of many misfortunes, turned into a newborn dragon with the potential to finally be truly free and reshape the very reality he now resided in. Escaped from the grasp of higher powers and not keen to be another cog in the machine once more, he uses all his cumulative knowledge and his new talents to survive and carve his own path to follow.

He did however not escape from misfortune, higher beings keen on interfering with his existence, his own instincts and impulses as a dragon contradicting his human mind, even old problems and afflictions he thought he had left behind come to haunt him. This is a story of exploring identity, the self, the world and everything in between.

Things to expect:
- A very complex magic system
- An original take on classic fantasy elements and beings
- A complex exploration of identity, mentality, nature versus nurture and so much more.
- A powerful main character that earns his place and forms his unique style
- Lots of contemplation and a slightly unhinged and scientific approach to studying magic.

I hope you enjoy the ride.

Sable didn’t know what she had expected from the afterlife, but turning into a giant flying lizard hadn’t been it.

And sure, she’s been thrust into a magic-crammed fantasy world with an obscenely powerful body, but things aren’t all great, here. There’s hordes of orcs to the north, an immortal legion of undead to the south, and fourteen human kingdoms who want the first dragon in centuries to be offed sooner than yesterday—except they’re too busy warring with each other to spare the resources. 

Good for her?

And what’s up with the [Levels], [Classes], and [Skills] stuff? Specifically, her [Hoard] and [Notoriety] stats. She gets stronger the more gold she has? The more people are terrified of her? No wonder the human kingdoms want her head on a spike, with motivations like those. Dragons in the past must have been seriously unsavory sorts. Maybe she can find less … evil … ways to progress? 

What are the odds taxes and propaganda can get her where she needs to be? Protection in exchange for tithes, and campaigns to make her seem scarier than she is?

That would make her a politician, wouldn’t it? A giant flying lizard politician.

What a headache.

The Immigrant Realm.  A crossroads between magical domains.  A place where heroes from the Greek legends, fairies from Avalon, and youkai from the Realms of Illusion, can meet, trade, and hide from people who want them dead.  Exiled witch Helena Aoede falls in the last group, having fled her home in Thebes after angering Apollo.  Now she lives in the ghetto, trying to scrape together rent money.

So when she's called on to help solve a supernatural murder case, she leaps at the chance.  But what was supposed to be a simple consultation rapidly escalates into a blood feud with the 'Living Dragon,' a magician backed by an unstoppable undead monster.  Now she's caught in a magical gang war, with only a clueless undead martial artist as backup.

Life was so much easier when she could just turn people into pigs.

Alt title: How to Dragon 101

Kill. Eat. Evolve. Repeat.

Jade was born wrong, as a magicless half-beastkin in a world ruled by power.

After a failed elven ritual traps her in a monster-filled dungeon, restraint stops mattering. She wakes up with scales, wings, and a body that grows stronger with every kill. The hunt feels good. Almost too good.

The only catch is that she’s becoming a dragon, in mind and body.

To escape, Jade must climb the dungeon’s food chain, indulging the instincts she spent her life suppressing, or die as prey. After all, humanity is optional. Survival isn’t.

What to expect:

- A monster evolution system, with Skills, Magic and Mutations
- This is a weak to strong story and Protagonist needs to sharpen her skills instead of just making numbers go up.
- Combat, power-ups, unique skills and mutation merges for powerful abilities

Some girls are reborn as chosen heroes. She was reborn as the thing heroes are sent to kill.

Waking up with scales, claws, and the overwhelming urge to steal treasure wasn't exactly the second chance at life she'd hoped for. But Barjuchne, the last dragon, the legendary terror, the creature every kingdom on the continent wants dead, is hers now.

And she is done being small.

Gold fuels her evolution. Gems sharpen her scales. Every level she climbs pulls her further from the frightened human she was and closer to something ancient, powerful, and magnificent. The world wants her destroyed?

Let them come.

But there's just one thing nobody warned her about regarding reincarnating in a magical world as a dragon.

The princesses.

She's collecting those too, now. Mostly by accident. Mostly.

Whether she's stumbling through stammered confessions or accidentally declaring war with a misread gesture, her hoard of remarkable suitors keeps growing, and somewhere between protecting her treasure and protecting them, the most terrifying thing imaginable is happening:

They might be falling for her.

[I was reborn as the world's last treasure hoarding dragon with an instinct to collect princesses... but I'm actually super socially awkward?!]
